title: Colorado ex parte renewal share, August 2026
question: What percentage of Colorado Medicaid and CHIP beneficiaries with a renewal due in August 2026 will CMS report as renewed on an ex parte basis in the first published original (O) submission row?
resolutionSource: CMS, State Medicaid and CHIP Eligibility Processing Data (data.medicaid.gov)
resolutionRule: Resolves to Colorado's ex parte renewal share for the August 2026 reporting period, computed from the original (O) submission row in CMS dataset 5abea2e0-3f8e-4b49-a50d-d63d5fd9103c when CMS first publishes it. Calculate 100 times Beneficiaries Whose Coverage Was Renewed on an Ex Parte Basis divided by Beneficiaries with a Renewal Due, using numerator and denominator as first published, rounded to one decimal. Subsequent revisions and updated (U) submissions do not change resolution.
drivers: Persistence near the recent Colorado original-submission level
Original-report backlog and processing disruption risk

reasoning.text: Colorado August 2026 original-submission ex parte renewal share

The target is Colorado's state row, not a national total or weighted average. Dataset 5abea2e0-3f8e-4b49-a50d-d63d5fd9103c distinguishes original (O) from updated (U) reports. All historical anchors use O rows. CMS's June 2025 snapshot state table defines the ex parte percentage relative to beneficiaries due for renewal, confirming numerator metric 5a1 and denominator metric 5. The forecast resolves on the first published August 2026 O row.

reasoning.call: Fetch CMS dataset through its public API with Colorado, O, and reporting_period >= 202507 filters; audit excerpt 1 of the single successful 12-row response.
Audit excerpt 2 of the same successful CMS API response, covering October-December 2025 original rows.
Audit excerpt 3 of the same successful CMS API response, covering January-June 2026 original rows.

reasoning.text: The base rate is the recent Colorado O-row reference class. January-June 2026 has an unrounded mean of 59.0635%, while the latest level is 60.7934%. The twelve fetched monthly observations also reveal an October 2025 disruption: pending renewals reached 35.8239% of those due, compared with 4.0902% in June 2026. That episode remains in the dispersion sample.

Publication-date validation limitation: the official CMS snapshot page lists May 2026 released August 28, April released July 31, and March released June 26, but does not provide a future August 2026 announcement schedule. The registered resolutionDate 2026-12-15 is retained as a contract field and could not be verified in this run; this output therefore does not satisfy the mandatory date-verification requirement. An ancillary monthly-reports page fetch returned an accessibility error. Further source lookups stopped; the numerical forecast uses the successful history fetch.

Prior/update/interval: Use a persistence prior shrunk equally toward the January-June 2026 mean. Level = 60.7934%; mean-reversion adjustment = -0.8650 percentage points; momentum, one-off point adjustment, and policy-mechanism adjustment each = 0. January-June average monthly change is only +0.0139 points, and no opened official evidence supports a Colorado policy shift. For an unconditional interval, retain all twelve July 2025-June 2026 O observations, including the backlog episode. The sample standard deviation of their eleven successive unrounded changes gives sigma = 10.4170 percentage points. A one-month normal half-width is 1.28*10.4170 = 13.3338 points. Scaling by sqrt(2) for June-to-August gives 18.8568 points, yielding final bounds 41.1% to 78.8%.

Each historical share = 100*ex_parte/renewal_due. Point = 0.5*60.7933719 + 0.5*59.0634588 = 59.9284153%, rounded to 59.9%. Sigma uses sample standard deviation with divisor 10 across eleven successive changes. Interval = 59.9284153 +/- 1.28*10.4170074*sqrt(2) = [41.0716177, 78.7852130], rounded to [41.1, 78.8].

The upside risk is substantially better automatic eligibility matching or a cohort unusually easy to renew without forms. The downside risk is delayed processing, a larger unresolved cohort, or ex parte outcomes classified as form-based renewals. A recurrence of October 2025's 39.3% original share would land below the interval. A broad automation improvement lifting the share above 78.8% would be outside the interval on the upside. These are scenarios, not verified current developments.
